data.title: Mic Issue
data.description:
The new iPhone 8 plus offers a set of microphones to ensure your iPhone makes the best out of the audio inputs it receives. The iPhone offers the users a mono speaker and microphone to ensure the best listening experience for their users. However, it is often reported by iPhone 8 plus users that, they are getting trouble regarding the microphones in their phones.

The most common issues reported in Apple’s user community forum and other blogs are:

  • Low or unclear voice sound in voice calls/ voice memos.
  • Low or unclear voice in Facetime, skype, or video recording.
  • Muffled or cracked sound while recording/calling using the mic.
  • Siri doesn’t work/ can’t hear me/ can’t pick up commands.

The iPhone 8 plus has at least 3 different microphones in different places for phones for different purposes.

  • The bottom of the phone, the left speaker grill is the mic for voice calls
  • One near your proximity sensor, used for voice commands for Siri
  • The one in the back of your in the camera square. There is a tiny hole for the mic to pick up audio input while recording a video.

Now your microphone issue may be caused by any of the one or all 3 microphones not working. There are some DIY (Do it yourself) fixes to try before you come to a decision.

  • Make sure if you use a protective cover for your phone. It doesn’t obstruct any speaker grills or mic holes.
  • Clear the phone to check and make sure there isn’t any debris in there.
  • Try recording your voice in a voice memo to make sure the mic works
  • If the mic works in voice memo make sure the app you are running has permission to use the microphone of your iPhone 8 plus go to: Settings > Privacy > Microphone and make sure the app is listed there for it to use the microphone.

data.title: Liquid Damage
data.description:
The new iPhone 8 plus is not a standard IP68 rated, dust and water-resistant phone. Which means it can not resist dust and water coming in up to it. However, it can resist certain levels of water. Apple has introduced a new technology called LCI. LCI is an abbreviation for liquid contact indicator. It is located in the sim tray region. Now you can see the LCI when you remove the sim tray, buy putting the ejector pin into the sim tray ejection hole. Once you have removed the sim tray, you should see a white/red portion inside the sim tray region. That is your LCI on the iPhone. If the LCI is completely white or silver then it is okay. The phone hasn’t contacted any water.

However, if your LCI turns red you can safely assume that it has been in touch with water and has taken in some water damage.

  • If you have dropped your phone in the water here are some basic things you should do:
  • Rinse your phone with a lens cloth or a microfiber cloth
  • You may gently tap the phone with the charger hole against your hand. It may drip the water out if it has gotten in there.
  • NEVER CHARGE YOUR PHONE UNTIL YOU HAVE MADE SURE IT IS COMPLETELY DRY
  • If anything spills on your phone other than water (like oil etc.) just rinse the place with a lint-free cloth.
  • If water has gotten into your phone, it may damage your Battery, Charging port, or give you muffled speakers.

data.title: Fingerprint Issue
data.description:
Apple has introduced an exclusive feature of Touch ID since the iPhone 5s. It is a fingerprint sensor that lets users of the iPhone 8 plus unlock their iPhone without having to put in a passcode every time they do so. Touch ID can be used as a payment method for Apple services and is a very secure way of ensuring payments too. However, like all the other technical difficulties you may face in your iPhone; your fingerprint/touch-id may cause an error in its operation. The touch ID problem is quite a common problem seen in the iPhone’s list of problems.

The most common issues faced regarding touch ID are:

  • You are asked to enter the passcode to unlock the phone by default instead of Touch ID
  • You can not avail of Apple Payment by touch-ID.
  • Can’t Register Touch ID to set up your fingerprint.
  • Touch ID is grayed or dimmed out.

Apple recommends some fixes you may try in your home which may fix the issue if it is due to a software glitch. Those fixes are:

  • Make sure your hands are clean and dry. Different sorts of moisturizers may affect the workability of your iPhone. (Such as Oil, lotion, sweat, or water)
  • Make sure your iPhone touch ID is clean and wipe it down with a lint-free cloth.
  • Make sure you put your entire finger on the home button to make the sensor work.
  • Make sure your screen protector or case is not getting in the way of touch ID
  • Update your iOS

Also, make sure that Touch ID does not work if you have...

  • Restarted your phone
  • You haven’t unlocked your device in 48 hours
  • 5 failed attempts to unlock the phone through touch ID.

If your error can’t be categorized or resolved through selective issues and prescribed fixes, you may need to get your phone checked by professional repairmen. data.description:

  • Volume down (-) button
  • Ringer Switch
  • Power Button
  • Home button

It does not have a Face ID or a face unlock feature. Now with time, the buttons of your iPhone 8 plus may face wear and tear and may cease to function properly. The most common issues faced regarding the buttons of smartphones are:

  • The Sound doesn’t increase/decrease when I press the volume up or down key.
  • The buttons are stuck and can’t be pressed
  • The switch doesn’t work/automatically switches between ringer and silent mode
  • Home button doesn’t work/unlock the phone.

These are the most common issues regarding the physical buttons in the smartphone. However, Apple recommends restarting the device and updating the iOS in this case. And if it still does not fix the issues, it needs to be getting looked at by professionals. iPhone recommends using Assistive touch for the longevity of the physical buttons of the iPhone 8 plus.

data.description:
The No light on Display issue of the iPhone 8 plus is where the user can’t see what’s happening on the phone. The phone runs okay. The phone vibrates and the user can hear the notification sounds and other inputs. But the problem is they can not see any of it because the phone display is just plain black. But the phone will respond or might even have incoming calls.

  • The key symptoms of the “No light on Display” issues are:
  • The Phone display boots up with an Apple logo but doesn’t get past the black screen.
  • The phone has calls, notifications but doesn’t show anything on display

This “No light on display” is usually an internal issue with the LCD connector. However, Apple recommends some processes to practice on your phone to make sure the black screen is not a software glitch.

Force Restart your iPhone.

Connect the lightning cable, charge it for 10 minutes. Then try force restarting the iPhone.

UNCONVENTIONAL: But press the screen into the phone so it may reconnect any dislodged LCD connector. This fix is not recommended however it resolved a lot of the user's Black Display issue.
